title: Troubleshoot alarm 626 tool pocket slide error on a Haas tool changer
scope: Alarm 626 troubleshooting as demonstrated in SRC_HAAS_0008.

context.subsystem: tool changer - tool pocket up/down travel
symptoms: tool pocket fails to reach the proper up/down position

subsystem.note: The narration says 'tool pocket' and 'carousel' but never names the tool changer style; team label.

symptoms.note: Stated in the narration (cue 1) and shown on the control.

alarm_codes.note: Stated in the narration and shown as '626 TOOL-POCKET SLIDE ERROR' on the control.

context.text: The presenter says alarm 626 occurs when the tool pocket failed to reach the proper up and down location.
context.explanation: The captions state this directly. Cue 1 is corrected from 'up in' to 'up and' (same transcript says 'pocket up and down').

observation.text: The control shows a list of active alarms and a red banner reading '626 TOOL-POCKET SLIDE ERROR'.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Control screen: Active Alarms list and a red banner '626 TOOL-POCKET SLIDE ERROR'.
evidence.explanation: The frame is of the control screen and the banner text is legible.

observation.explanation: The presenter names this alarm at the start of the video.

action.text: The presenter says to press the recovery button and follow the instruction to recover the tool change.
An 'Automatic Recovery' dialog on the control reads 'Waiting for the pocket to push up'.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Control screen with an 'Automatic Recovery' dialog reading 'Waiting for the pocket to push up'.
evidence.explanation: The dialog title and its first line of text are legible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about pressing the recovery button and following the instruction.

acceptance_criteria.text: The presenter says to command several tool changes to make sure the tool change is working correctly.
acceptance_criteria.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected from 'several - changes' (same sentence ends 'make sure the tool change is working correctly').

questions.question: Why is the recovery button the first thing to try before inspecting anything?

steps.title: Inspect the pocket, carousel and air supply

condition.text: The presenter says to follow these troubleshooting steps if the machine is still getting alarm 626.

action.text: The presenter says to give the pocket and carousel a good look for loose or damaged components.
The presenter says to make sure the machine has sufficient air pressure and volume during the tool change.
A pressure gauge is mounted on a panel of solenoid valves and air lines, beside an 'AIR - LUBRICATION' diagram label.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Pneumatics panel with an air pressure gauge and a bank of solenoid valves, beside an 'AIR - LUBRICATION' diagram label.
evidence.explanation: The gauge, valves and tubing are visible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about air pressure and volume.

action.text: The presenter says to look at the air line to the pocket air cylinder, and to look for kinks or broken lines.
A pneumatic cylinder with a thin air line is mounted in a cast housing.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Close-up of a pneumatic cylinder with a thin air line, mounted in a cast housing.
evidence.explanation: The cylinder body, its rod and the air line are visible in the frame; the frame alone does not show which cylinder this is.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about the air line to the pocket air cylinder.

rationale.text: The presenter says low air can prevent the tool pocket from reaching the proper position.

questions.question: What pressure counts as sufficient air pressure and volume?

steps.title: Check the pocket up and down proximity switches

action.text: The presenter says to examine the pocket up and down proximity switches and look for contamination or damage.
The presenter says to touch the face of each switch with a small flat blade screwdriver.

acceptance_criteria.text: The presenter says the switch should change state when its face is touched.

questions.question: Why does a switch that fails to change state point to the alarm?

steps.title: Test the pocket up and down solenoid

context.text: The presenter says a link in the video description shows how to test the solenoid and switches.

action.text: The presenter says to manually activate the pocket up and down solenoid, if possible, to verify that it is working correctly.
A thin tool tip is pressed into a recess on the face of a solenoid valve.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Close-up of a solenoid valve with a thin tool tip pressed into a recess on its face.
evidence.explanation: The tool tip and the valve's manual override are visible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about manually activating the solenoid.

acceptance_criteria.text: The presenter says to make sure the pocket up and down switches change state at the appropriate time.

questions.question: The captions say 'if possible': when is manual activation not possible?

steps.title: Contact the service outlet if the alarm persists

condition.text: The presenter says this applies if the machine is still getting alarm 626 after these checks.
condition.explanation: The captions state this directly. Cue 13 is corrected from 'ha spectra outlet' to 'HFO' (the description says 'contact your local HFO').

action.text: The presenter says to contact your HFO.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected as above.

questions.question: What does the HFO do next, and what should be reported to them?

claim.text: The presenter treats the inspection steps as what to do if alarm 626 continues after recovery and several test tool changes.
